title: Allocator fair-share reservation leak causing reserved-pool headroom exhaustion
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers experienced sudden 503s and rejected allocations during concurrent burst traffic. Symptoms included reserved-pool headroom hitting zero despite visible idle GPUs and queued requests being starved. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and a permanent fix for a reservation accounting leak in the allocator's fair-share path.
root_cause: A race in the allocator's fair-share reservation flow: when queued requests were preempted and later re-queued during leader handoff, the reservation decrement path was skipped in a failure branch. That left ephemeral reservations counted against reserved-pool headroom. Over a period of sustained burst traffic this gradually exhausted burst credits/headroom for affected pools, causing abrupt allocation failures for tenants with reserved capacity. The bug was introduced by an earlier optimization that split reservation bookkeeping across async callbacks without an atomic invariant.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: enable emergency fallback to strict FIFO allocation for impacted pools and reduce per-pool burst ceiling to prevent further headroom exhaustion (config toggle applied globally for 30m windows). 2) Short-term: force reconciliation job to run across all reserved pools every 2 minutes to detect and clear stale reservations. 3) Customer-level: open support tickets for impacted tenants, apply temporary manual credits to pools where appropriate.
fix_plan: Add an atomic reservation transact API so reservation increments and decrements are always paired in the same Raft transaction
Remove async split-decrement path and route all reservation state changes through the new transact API
Add instrumentation and a 'stale_reservation' metric with alerting (threshold > 10 stale/reservations/min)
Backfill reconciliation job to be safe-by-default for 48 hours after rollout
Canary rollout on staging then on low-traffic region, then global
test_plan: Unit tests for reservation transact API (happy/failure/retry paths), integration test that simulates leader handoff mid-reservation using our testrunner, chaos test that injects preemption failures, and a load test verifying no headroom leak at 10k concurrent burst requests.

2026-03-08 02:32 UTC - Triage: observed reserved pool headroom=0 while GPUs idled; began allocation path tracing
2026-03-08 03:10 UTC - Hotfix applied: enabled FIFO fallback for affected pools and kicked reconciliation job (reduced error rate to baseline)
2026-03-09 09:00 UTC - Root cause narrowed to allocator fair-share branch after reproducer in local cluster
2026-03-10 16:20 UTC - Patch implemented (atomic transact API) and unit tests added
2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Canary rollout to staging and one low-traffic region; metrics look healthy

postmortem_actions: Ship reservation transact API and roll to all regions (runtime-1.22)
Add reconciliation runbook and automate running after leader change events
Add guardrails in autoscaler: detect sustained headroom decline with non-increasing 'gpu_utilization' and trigger safe-fallback
Run a simulated leader-handoff regression test in nightly CI
Review async callbacks across allocator codepaths and eliminate split state changes
customer_comms: Support brief sent to impacted tenants summarizing cause, immediate mitigations applied, estimated timeline for permanent fix, and a one-time credit offer. Customer-facing postmortem to be published after final rollout. Account managers are greenlit to schedule follow-ups for critical customers.
notes: This regression surfaced after performance work to reduce allocation tail latency. The optimization was valid for the common case but broke the invariant on edge-case leader preemption. We should prioritize invariant-based code reviews for allocator changes going forward. Consider adding an allocator simulation harness to catch similar races earlier.
